policy_title: Ban Fracking and New Coal Mines
stated: Maintaining the ban on fracking and introducing a ban on new coal mines.

source.quote: Maintaining the ban on fracking and introducing a ban on new coal mines.

bearing_set.reason: Banning fracking and new coal mines directly restricts fossil fuel extraction, bearing materially on UK emissions trajectory and local air/water quality impacts.

Fracking ban forgoes potential domestic gas supply that could exert downward pressure on wholesale gas prices and energy bills — the mechanism (domestic shale supply → gas market price → household energy costs) is concrete and genuinely contested among credible analysts, giving O2 a real, mixed/contested verdict.

The bans foreclose domestic fossil-fuel development, creating a genuine contested tradeoff: near-term restriction on energy-sector investment and output vs. long-term redirection toward cleaner, more durable energy infrastructure — the dual-horizon effect on real living standards and energy security earns a real verdict here.

membership_note: O2 (energy bills) was considered but mainstream economic analysis (e.g. OBR, Ofgem) holds that UK shale output would not materially move consumer gas prices, which are globally determined — the mechanism is too weak for a non-negligible verdict. O12 and O4 effects (tax revenues, mining jobs) are real but negligible given how small/nonexistent current UK shale and coal production are. O6 and O13 are the genuine bearings.
